headline: Chips and Software Lead a Tech-Driven Midday Advance
body_html:
Stocks are leaning higher at midday, with 319 of the 544 names we track advancing and 223 declining. Prices are not final, but the tone is constructive, and the gains are being driven by technology rather than spread evenly across the market.

Semiconductors are the clear front-runner, up 1.62%, with software next at 0.96%. Credo Technology has climbed 6.27% on the connectivity side of the chip trade. Datadog, the standout mover, is up 7.1%, and Zscaler has added 5.53%. Energy (up 0.69%) and industrials (up 0.61%) are also in the green, and Bloom Energy is up 6.21% within energy.

The weakness sits mainly in consumer names, down 0.74% as a group, while homebuilders are off 0.37% and materials 0.13%. Healthcare is slightly lower, down 0.11%, held back by DexCom, off 5.42%, and Stryker, off 3.3%. Into the close, watch whether chip and software leadership holds, whether gainers stay ahead of decliners, and how oil-sensitive shares react to stalled Iran-US diplomacy ahead of Thursday's open.

briefs.headline: Datadog Pops as Software Firms Up
briefs.body: Datadog is the standout mover at midday, up 7.1% and leading the observability corner of software. Zscaler is up 5.53% in security, helping lift the group 0.96%. Pegasystems, down 4.03%, is a reminder that the rally is selective within the sector.

briefs.headline: Credo Rides the Chip Tape Higher
briefs.body: Credo Technology is up 6.27%, one of the sharpest gains in a semiconductor group that is up 1.62% and leading all eight sectors we track. The strength points to continued appetite for the hardware behind AI data centers, though midday prices can still shift.

briefs.headline: Neocloud Doubts Meet Pricing Pushback
briefs.body: Investors are questioning the business model of the so-called neoclouds, yet Nebius argues that prices for AI computing are rising. Separately, OpenAI is extending ads in ChatGPT to 26 more countries, another sign of the push to diversify revenue.

briefs.headline: Medical Device Names Slide
briefs.body: DexCom is down 5.42% and Stryker is down 3.3%, making devices the weak spot in a healthcare group that is off 0.11%. Charles River Labs offers a counterpoint, up 6.98% and among the day's top gainers, so the weakness is far from sector-wide.

briefs.headline: Consumer Split: RVs Up, Drinks and Coffee Down
briefs.body: Consumer shares are the weakest group, down 0.74%, but the picture is mixed. Winnebago is up 6.95%, while Dutch Bros has lost 4.02% and Celsius Holdings 3.34%. Homebuilders, down 0.37%, add to the cautious tone for household-linked spending.

briefs.headline: Gulf Markets Dip as Iran-US Talks Stall
briefs.body: Most Gulf bourses are slipping as diplomacy between Iran and the US reaches a standstill. Data showing Saudi crude exports at a five-month high in August adds to the oil backdrop, with energy up 0.69% here. In London, hot inflation is reported to be outweighing an energy boost for the FTSE 100.
